acceptanceCriteria: Implements the C6.4 10-step algorithm in order; analyse never rejects; uses only res.status and res.text(); at most one fetch call per analyse; no SDK or other dependency
AC4 (a)-(n) at provider level incl. never() stub times out, thinking-first content, usage mapping, headers and URL (baseUrl + /v1/messages)
DES-1: a capture stub asserts init.redirect === 'error'; a 307 stub gives model_error/redirect_refused without calling text(); a stub throwing TypeError gives model_error/fetch_threw
RISK-10: model output with summary > 200 or suggestedReply > 1200 chars is rejected (invalid_output) before validateTriage/V2; a 32k-char 'a.a.a.' payload returns fallback in < 100 ms
completedWork: src/triage/anthropic-provider.js (zero deps, CommonJS) exports createAnthropicProvider({apiKey, model, baseUrl, timeoutMs, maxTokens, fetchImpl}) -> {model, analyse}. analyse follows C6.4 in order: (1) buildRequestBody inside the try, so its TypeError (t04 note) becomes model_error/fetch_threw with no fetch call; (2) AbortController + setTimeout(timeoutMs); (3) one fetchImpl(baseUrl + '/v1/messages', {method:'POST', headers:{content-type, x-api-key, anthropic-version:2023-06-01}, body: JSON.stringify(body), signal, redirect:'error'}), and then res.text(), each raced against the abort signal (a never-settling stub still times out); abort -> timeout/'timeout', any other throw (incl. sync throw, non-function fetchImpl, non-object response or non-integer status) -> model_error/fetch_threw; timer cleared in finally; abort listeners removed after settle; (4) 3xx -> model_error/redirect_refused without reading the body, other non-2xx -> model_error/http_<status> (body read under the timeout, per step order); (5) unparseable or non-object body -> model_error/body_not_json; (6) stop_reason refusal -> refusal/'refusal', max_tokens -> truncated/'max_tokens'; (7) first content element with type 'text' and string text (thinking skipped) else invalid_output/no_text_block; (8) text not JSON -> invalid_output/text_not_json; RISK-10 gate: if summary is a string > 200 chars or suggestedReply a string > 1200 chars -> invalid_output/invalid:<summary_v1|reply_length> (the same codes, in the same order, validateTriage itself reports for such output) without calling validateTriage; (9) validateTriage -> invalid_output/invalid:<codes> or {ok:true, triage (enums normalised), upstreamStatus, usage}; (10) usage {inputTokens, outputTokens} when both are numbers, else null, attached to every result where the body was parsed. upstreamStatus is the HTTP status once known, else null. detail is always a fixed code; no content is echoed (tested with a canary). test/unit/anthropic-provider.test.js: 25 tests (headers/URL/redirect/signal/body capture; AC4 a-n; DES-1 for 300-399 with a no-read stub that counts text()/json() calls (FND-1); sync throw; text() rejection; timeouts on fetch and on the body read, and abort-rejecting fetch; timer cleared; usage mapping; buildRequestBody guard; canary non-echo; RISK-10 32k payload < 100 ms and limit boundaries 200/201 and 1200/1201; never-rejects sweep). RISK-10 resolved at the call site: probe ev:ev-muypnaj3-01d37d63 shows ungated validateTriage takes 8301 ms on the 32k 'a.a.a.' output while gated analyse takes 1.87 ms with the identical detail 'invalid:summary_v1,reply_length'.
remainingIssues: RISK-10 is resolved only at this call site. schema.js validateTriage/validateResponse are unchanged (approved phase), so any other caller that validates unbounded text (e.g. t08 eval/run.js calling validateResponse on fallback or live results, t15 contract tests) still has the quadratic V2 cost; fallback output is bounded (<= 600-char templates) so the eval's fallback path is not exposed. Recommend the schema owner add the length gate inside schema.js in a later revision (the review's original recommendation).

Usage/latency logging: per C6.4 the provider has no logger and returns usage in LiveResult; latency is measured and logged by service.js (t10) via AnalysisMeta and the D1.6 request log. The provider itself logs nothing, so no prompt content can leak from it.

Interpretation within the contract: a buildRequestBody TypeError (invalid model/maxTokens/non-string ticket) and a malformed response object (null, non-integer status) map to model_error/fetch_threw, the C6.4 catch-all ('any other throw'), since the fixed detail list has no closer code. A JSON body that parses to a non-object (e.g. 'null') maps to model_error/body_not_json. Non-2xx, non-3xx bodies are read (under the timeout) before http_<status> is returned, following the step order; if that read fails the result is fetch_threw/timeout with the status.
createAnthropicProvider does not validate opts at creation (config.js validates them); invalid values surface as model_error or timeout at analyse time.
Not tested: no live Anthropic call (no API key). Results here are evidence about the pipeline against stubs, not about model behaviour or real API shape drift (RISK-7 remains open until a live call).
Not tested here: real-fetch behaviour with redirect:'error' against fake-anthropic 307 (AC4 o end-to-end) - that is t15's spawned-server test; the provider-level stub tests cover the contract.
